extraction.name: Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations
extraction.description: The Visual Genome dataset is a large-scale dataset designed to enable the modeling of relationships and interactions between objects in images for cognitive tasks. It contains over 100,000 images densely annotated with objects, attributes, relationships, region descriptions, scene graphs, and question-answer pairs.
extraction.creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bernstein, Li Fei-Fei
extraction.citeAs: Krishna, R., Zhu, Y., Groth, O., Johnson, J., Hata, K., Kravitz, J., Chen, S., Kalantidis, Y., Li, L.J., Shamma, D.A., Bernstein, M.S., Fei-Fei, L. (2016). Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected and verified entirely by crowd workers from Amazon Mechanical Turk. The process involved multiple stages including collecting region descriptions, extracting objects, attributes, and relationships, creating region and scene graphs, and generating question-answer pairs. Verification was conducted using majority voting and rapid judgments.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The dataset uses 108,249 images from the intersection of the YFCC100M and MS-COCO datasets. These are real-world, non-iconic images uploaded onto Flickr by users.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The dataset was collected over the course of 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases in region descriptions and question-answer pairs were canonicalized to WordNet synsets to reduce ambiguity and connect concepts across images.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Region descriptions were preprocessed by removing non-alphanumeric characters, lowercasing, and stripping whitespace. Bounding boxes were drawn to satisfy coverage and quality requirements. Objects were extracted using Stanford's dependency parser and verified by workers. Canonicalization involved mapping terms to WordNet synsets using lexeme counts and hand-crafted rules.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd workers on Amazon Mechanical Turk performed annotations. Tasks included drawing bounding boxes for regions and objects, writing region descriptions, extracting objects/attributes/relationships from descriptions, and writing question-answer pairs. Verification was done via majority voting (3 workers) or rapid judgments for objects.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Verification strategies included majority voting and rapid judgments to eliminate incorrect, vague, subjective, or opinionated annotations. Precision and recall scores were calculated for canonicalization mappings.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each image has an average of 42 region descriptions, 21 objects, 16 attributes, 18 relationships, and 17 question-answer pairs.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 33,000 unique workers contributed. 93.02% were from the United States. The age range was 18-68, with the majority between 25 and 34. The gender split was 54.15% male and 45.85% female.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford CoreNLP (dependency parser), Stanford NLP tools (for noun phrase extraction), WordNet (for canonicalization)
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to enable comprehensive scene understanding and cognitive tasks like image description and question answering, moving beyond simple perceptual tasks.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is biased towards images of people and sports (e.g., skiing, surfing) due to the source images from Flickr. There is also a geographic bias in annotators, with 93% from the US.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset contains real-world images which may have varying quality. Canonicalization mappings are not perfect and contain some ambiguity. The dataset is biased towards certain object categories and relationships.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and benchmarking computer vision models for tasks such as object detection, attribute prediction, relationship prediction, region description generation, visual question answering, and semantic image retrieval.
